messages:
matt: grabbing perfetto trace for kv-cache hot path, a bunch of kernels show up with no source lines. looks like symbols missing for cupti/driver stuff. any ideas?
anya: can you paste the perfetto link and nsys capture?
matt: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (private) and uploaded nsys here: s3://redwood-debug/nsys/1998765432.nsight
perf-bot: capture uploaded: s3://redwood-debug/nsys/1998765432.nsight (size 420MB) :white_check_mark:
sanjay: first guess is CUPTI soname mismatch between container and host driver. common when we run a slim image that bundles a different libcupti or none at all. can you run inside container: `ldd /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so || true` and `readelf -a libcupti.so | grep SONAME`?
matt: running now, output: ```
ldd: not found
readelf: not found
``` so the container is scratchy minimal.
anya: ok that explains tools missing. did you also strip the runtime build? Dockerfile has `strip --strip-unneeded` in the final stage sometimes.
james: also check that the kernel module/driver version on host matches the CUDA/CUPTI headers used to build the binary. mismatched sonames cause symbol resolution to fall back and traces lose line mapping.
sanjay: short repro we use: `docker run --rm -v /tmp/profiles:/profiles --privileged -v /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/:/hostlibs:ro myimage /bin/bash -c "LD_PRELOAD=/hostlibs/libcupti.so perfetto ..."` bind-mounting the host cupti into container fixes a lot of cases.
anya: alternative is to install debug utils in the container: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y binutils readelf` then verify lib matches host with `sha256sum /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` vs host.
matt: i tried bind-mounting libcupti from host and retook trace. new perfetto shows source lines for the previously blank kernels. nice.
perf-bot: new capture uploaded: s3://redwood-debug/nsys/1998765489.nsight
james: if you want a more permanent fix, add a debug-profiling target in CI that builds an image with cupti from the matching cuda package and without strip. e.g. keep a `*-debug` image we use only for perf runs.
anya: also worth adding a quick check in our profiling docs: warn about stripped binaries and missing /usr/lib/nvidia*/libcupti.so in containers. a 1-liner repro + bind-mount example will save time.
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-1123 to add a `perf-debug` flavor and a short runbook.
matt: rolling patch: update runbook and add `--volume /usr/lib/nvidia:/hostnvidia:ro` to perf job template. verified traces now have complete lineinfo. thanks all :tada:
